transitions.summary: Wording only, on Konami's period rulings (round 036). The era text "This card can only be Special Summoned from your Extra Deck by removing from play the above cards you control." says "can only be", not "cannot be Special Summoned except by". Konami's rulebook (Versions 7.0 to 8.0) lets a Special Summon Monster be Special Summoned by another card's effect once it was properly Special Summoned first, and Konami's strategy article (printed 2009-12-07) applies that to "can only be Special Summoned by" wording and keeps the permanent lock for "except by". So the era card and the errata'd "Must first be Special Summoned (from your Extra Deck) by banishing the above cards you control." revive alike. The same printing rewrites the discard effect into PSCT with explicit targeting; this record's earlier reading called only the revival a behavioural difference, and no period ruling read here addresses the targeting, so none is established or adjudicated by this correction. No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

rulings_check.difference: The era discard effect ('You can discard 1 card to change the battle position of 1 monster your opponent controls') targeted, or did not target, where the 2018 wording says 'then target 1 monster your opponent controls'.

Round 036 (2026-09-29) correction. This record's strict-nomi call ("can only be Special Summoned" read as a permanent lock) was read from the printed wording alone and cited no period ruling. Konami's rulebook, Versions 7.0 (capture 2008-12-30), 7.1 (2010-03-30), 7.2 (2011-05-16) and 8.0 (linked from Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18), says of Special Summon Monsters: "You cannot use a card effect to Special Summon those monsters from your hand, Deck, or the Graveyard unless it was properly Special Summoned first." Konami's TCG strategy article (printed date 2009-12-07; earliest capture 2015-11-06) says a monster worded "This card can only be Special Summoned by..." can be Special Summoned again from the Graveyard after one proper Summon, and reserves the permanent lock for "cannot be Special Summoned except by...". Konami's Extreme Victory card rulings (compiled 2011-05-12, version 1.2; listed on Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18) rule, for a card whose text is "This card can only be Special Summoned by controlling 3 or more face-up "Meklord" monsters": "If you Special Summon this card correctly, it can later be Special Summoned back from the Graveyard." This card's text says "can only be" and none of its printed texts says "except", so the era card and the errata'd card revive alike. For its contact-Fusion sibling the UDE/Konami card FAQ (Konami-hosted 2008-12-15, page U-Z) rules: "Once properly Summoned by the method written in the text this card can be Special Summoned from the Graveyard with effects like "Call of the Haunted" or "Re-Fusion"" ("VWXYZ-Dragon Catapult Cannon"), and Konami's strategy article says Fusion monsters that say "You do not use "Polymerization"" "follow the same rules as monsters like "Chaos Sorcerer" that say "This card can only be Special Summoned by..."". The card itself has no FAQ entry. Not adjudicated: whether the era discard effect targeted, which the era text does not say and the record's earlier reading did not call a difference (open question for the owner, round 036 report). Evidence and its limits: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, sections 3 and 6.9 and the round-036 section. Not established: the Graveyard-revival answer for GOAT (2005-04-01), which is out of this record's scope. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: 'This card can only be Special Summoned from your Extra Deck by removing from play the above cards you control' becomes 'Must first be Special Summoned (from your Extra Deck) by banishing the above cards you control'. The period wording barred every Special Summon that was not that banish procedure, so the card could never be returned to the field once it left; the modern semi-Nomi wording allows any later Special Summon, revival from the Graveyard included, after the card has been properly Special Summoned once. The same printing also rewrote the discard effect into PSCT with explicit targeting ('You can discard 1 card to change the battle position of 1 monster your opponent controls' -> 'You can discard 1 card, then target 1 monster your opponent controls; change that target's battle position'), with the discard remaining an activation cost in both." Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In Edison the EDOPro card can be revived from the Graveyard by Monster Reborn, Call of the Haunted or Premature Burial after one proper summon, which the period Nomi text forbade entirely." Superseded coverage, kept verbatim: "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode" (gap_sources ignis-babelcdb, yugipedia-card-errata).

Round 037 (2026-09-29), part D. Round 036's open question, whether the era discard effect targeted, was searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents (the transition's rulings_check). No ruling names VW-Tiger Catapult, so the answer is unresolved at Edison and at Tengu and the cosmetic call stands. Two rulings on other cards bear on it and are recorded as not counted: the card FAQ says the first effect of the sibling 'VWXYZ-Dragon Catapult Cannon' targets, and Konami's Raging Battle ruling says the Trigger Effect of 'Blackwing - Elphin the Raven', worded 'change the Battle Position of 1 monster your opponent controls', targets the opponent's monster. Those point to the era effect having targeted, as the 2018 wording says, but neither is a ruling on this card; if a ruling says it did not target, the difference becomes a functional transition and a known gap.
